name: rct2-proximity-bonus-plan
description: RCT2 proximity excitement bonuses - full scoring table, the loop-under-lift recipe worth ~+0.86, and the turn-direction rule
metadata:

---

`BonusProximity` multiplier is 20130/65536 = **x0.307** on `ride_ratings_get_proximity_score`
(RideRatings.cpp ~1379). Raw score x 0.307 = rating units; 100 rating units = 1.00 excitement.

## Full payout table (RideRatings.cpp:1382-1408), best first
| Bonus | helper | hits to cap | excitement |
|---|---|---|---|
| TRACK_THROUGH_VERTICAL_LOOP | h2(+4, cap6, x20) | **2** | **+0.37** |
| INTERSECTING_VERTICAL_LOOP | h3(100) | **1** | **+0.31** |
| THROUGH_VERTICAL_LOOP | h2(+4, cap6, x10) | 2 | +0.18 |
| OWN_STATION_TOUCH_ABOVE | h3(55) | 1 | +0.17 |
| OWN_TRACK_TOUCH_ABOVE | h2(+10, cap15, x3.33) | 5 | +0.15 |
| OWN_TRACK_CLOSE_ABOVE | h1(cap5, x6) | 5 | +0.09 |
| OWN_STATION_CLOSE_ABOVE | h3(25) | 1 | +0.08 |
| SURFACE_TOUCH | h1(cap70, x1.71) | 70 | +0.37 but MEASURED DUD (see below) |

Loop bonuses stack: **0.37+0.31+0.18 = +0.86** from one well-placed crossing.

## MEASURED (round 3): SURFACE_TOUCH is NOT worth chasing
~60 ground-level elements added; excitement only 7.09 -> 7.12, and intensity 8.60 -> 9.08 from the
turns' lateral G ate the gain. Don't redo.

## The loop-under-lift recipe (round 4, designed but NOT finished - do this first next round)
Conditions (`ride_ratings_score_close_proximity_loops_helper`, line 634): for each vertical-loop
element the game scans the loop's own tile AND the tile in front. Another **track** element there
scores if `(dirA ^ dirB) & 1` (90 degrees) and `other.baseHeight - loopElement.baseHeight` in
**[0,16] units = [0,128] z**. If that other element is itself a vertical loop, INTERSECTING also fires.

The cheap way to satisfy it: **the lift hill already runs along x at y=60.** Put a ground-level
vertical loop travelling along +/-y so its footprint covers a `y=60` lift tile. No altitude
gymnastics needed - the loop stays on the ground and the lift is the perpendicular crossing element.

Verified round-4 numbers for the standard skeleton (station (60,60) dir 0, 4 station + 15 chain pieces):
- lift tiles x=42..56 at y=60; **lift top z=256 at x=41**; z(x) ~= 256 - (x-42)*9.6
- post-drop ground track is at **z=128** (not 112), cursor lands at (35,60,128) dir 0
- a loop based at z=128 tops out at **z=232** -> needs the lift above it, so target **x=42 or 43**
  (lift z ~256 / ~246). x=45+ is z<=228 and will collide.
- zDiff test passes easily: 256-128 = 128 z = exactly 16 units, and higher loop elements pass too.

## Turn direction rule (cost me round 4 - I guessed wrong)
**left turn => dir-1 mod 4; right turn => dir+1 mod 4.** dir 0=-x, 1=+y, 2=+x, 3=-y.
So from dir 2 (+x) you need `right_turn_3/5` to face dir 3 (-y). I used left_turn_3 and ended up at
dir 1 heading +y, which put the loop at y=67-71 - nowhere near the lift - and ran out of clock.
Rotating a piece delta from dir 0 to dir 3: `(dx,dy) -> (-dy, dx)`. left_vertical_loop is
(-2,-1) at dir 0, so **(+1,-2) at dir 3**.

## Also still untried
- `OWN_STATION_TOUCH_ABOVE`: fly track over a station tile at exactly **z=128** (station z=112,
  clearanceHeight 16). No perpendicular requirement - condition is just
  `stationElement.clearanceHeight == flyoverElement.baseHeight` (line 816). Cheap +0.17.

See [[rct2-twister-rating-levers]].

I recorded the full payout table, the verified skeleton geometry (lift top z=256 at x=41, post-drop ground at z=128, loop tops at 232 so the crossing must be at x=42-43), and the turn-direction rule to memory so rounds 5-6 can execute this in a few minutes instead of rediscovering it.

**Best coaster this round: the round-3 skeleton — 14-tile chain lift, 60° plunge, 3 vertical loops + 3 corkscrew pairs, ground-level serpentine return — 7.12 excitement / 9.08 intensity, similarity 0.338.**
